name: Public Health Foundations (books)
description: The textbook layer for a public health / global health expert: health policy and governance, health economics and financing, health systems and primary care, quality, equity and the social determinants, health promotion and behaviour change, qualitative methods, public health ethics, demography, preparedness and resilience. Complements ph-background (WHO reports and guidelines) and epi-methods (quantitative methodology). Most sources are open access; a few canonical texts are listed for you to obtain via your own library and drop into the folder.

sources.title: Disease Control Priorities 3rd ed, Vol 9 — Improving Health and Reducing Poverty
sources.note: Health economics, cost-effectiveness analysis and priority setting: the reference volume for deciding what a health system should buy.

sources.title: Organization and Financing of Public Health Services in Europe
sources.note: How public health is funded, organised and delivered across European systems.

sources.title: Implementing the Primary Health Care Approach: A Primer
sources.note: WHO/Observatory primer on the PHC approach — the organising model of modern health systems.

sources.title: Improving Healthcare Quality in Europe
sources.note: Quality strategies, their effectiveness and how they are implemented.

sources.title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About European Union Health Policy
sources.note: Health policy-making, governance and law at supranational level.

sources.title: The Role of Public Health Organizations in Addressing Public Health Problems in Europe
sources.note: Institutional design and the essential public health functions.

sources.title: Economic Crisis, Health Systems and Health in Europe: Country Experience
sources.note: Health system resilience and the health effects of austerity — natural-experiment evidence.

sources.title: Trends in Health Systems in the Former Soviet Countries
sources.note: Comparative health system transition across a whole region.

sources.title: Civil Society and Health: Contributions and Potential
sources.note: Civil society, participation and accountability in health.

sources.title: The Future of the Public's Health in the 21st Century
sources.note: IOM's foundational statement of the population-health framework and its determinants.

sources.title: Vibrant and Healthy Kids: Aligning Science, Practice and Policy to Advance Health Equity
sources.note: Health equity and the life-course/social-determinants evidence base.

sources.title: Evidence-Based Practice for Public Health Emergency Preparedness and Response
sources.note: Preparedness, response and the evidence behind emergency public health.

sources.title: Healthy, Resilient, and Sustainable Communities After Disasters
sources.note: Recovery, resilience and community health systems.

sources.title: Theory at a Glance: A Guide for Health Promotion Practice (2nd ed) — US National Cancer Institute
sources.note: Behaviour-change and health-promotion theory: Health Belief Model, Stages of Change, Social Cognitive Theory, diffusion of innovations, and how to choose between them. US public domain.

sources.title: Qualitative Research: a practical guide for health and social care researchers and practitioners
sources.note: Qualitative methodology: study design, sampling, interviews and focus groups, thematic analysis, rigour and reflexivity. CC BY-NC (Monash University).

sources.title: Public Health Ethics: Global Cases, Practice, and Context (Barrett, Ortmann, Dawson et al., Springer)
sources.note: OPEN ACCESS, but Springer blocks scripted download — opening the DOI in a browser gives the free PDF. Public health ethics: the standard casebook (screening, surveillance, resource allocation, research ethics in LMICs).

sources.title: Making Health Policy (Buse, Mays & Walt, Open University Press) — latest edition
sources.note: Health policy analysis: the policy triangle (content/context/process/actors), agenda setting, power and interests, global health governance. The standard MPH policy text. Check the current edition in the ITG catalogue.

sources.title: Methods for the Economic Evaluation of Health Care Programmes (Drummond, Sculpher, Claxton et al., Oxford) — latest edition
sources.note: Health economics: cost-effectiveness, cost-utility and cost-benefit analysis, QALYs, decision-analytic modelling, handling uncertainty. ISBN is for the 4th ed — verify the current edition.

sources.title: Demography: Measuring and Modeling Population Processes (Preston, Heuveline & Guillot, Blackwell)
sources.note: Formal demography: life tables, standardisation, fertility and mortality measures, population projection, stable population theory — the arithmetic behind every denominator in public health.
